conventions: Status of rule-30 fusions in this chapter: a multi-morpheme fusion is recorded `aligned` wherever a rule fixes its source head — the morpheme carrying the rendering's lexeme (לָכֵן → *Therefore* on כֵּן, 34.10 and 34.25), the negation (rules 35 and 48: וְלֹא → *Neither* and *Nor*, 34.12 and 34.19; וְאֵין → *nor*, 34.22; לֹא בְ → *without*, 34.20 and 34.35 twice), the construct noun of a preposition-plus-construct compound (rule 23: לִפְנֵי → *more than*, 34.19), or the governing first preposition of a compound preposition (rule 23: מֵעִם → *as … wilt*, 34.33). It is recorded `noncompositional` only where no morpheme's own lexeme is uniquely written in the single English rendering and rule 6's deterministic first-token anchor is the sole basis for the source head: חֲצוֹת לָיְלָה → *midnight* (34.20) and אֲשֶׁר עַל־כֵּן → *Because* (34.27). The corpus records both statuses for one and the same fusion, so this is a recording convention for readers of this chapter and not a claim that the aligned fusions are divisible.

Head of a preposition unit that holds a recast clause's complementizer: this chapter heads it on the subordinating word, whatever else the unit also carries. The privative מִן takes *That … not* (34.30 s001) and *That there be none* (34.30 s005) and heads on *That* in both, as it heads on *that* at 34.10 where it holds the complementizer alone; the purpose לְ takes *So that* (34.28) and heads on *that*. A waw rendered by a coordinator and a subordinator written together still heads on the coordinator under rule 55 (*so that* at 34.25, *And when* at 34.29), so the two shapes are headed on opposite words and the difference is the morpheme, not the English.

Presentative negative frame in a privative clause: where a privative מִן is recast as a negative existential clause and no אַיִן or other negative morpheme stands in it, the whole supplied frame — *there be none* at 34.30 — joins the מִן unit, on the reasoning by which rule 50 gives the dummy and copula to the morpheme carrying the negation and rule 48 gives that negation to the מִן. Compare 34.22, where a written אַיִן takes *There is no* itself. Do not mark *there be* `added`: the negation is the preposition's own contribution and the frame is what English writes around it.
report: Read all 37 verses end to end against the 54-lemma candidate table and, separately, against an inventory of the 20 `added` units, which the table is blind to. No construction is analysed two ways with nothing in the source licensing the difference, so verdict no-change and patches empty.

Near misses resolved, each licensed by what the ASV wrote: לְ and עַל unrepresented at 34.3, 34.8, 34.22, 34.23 and 34.34, where the English takes a bare object or writes no function word (rules 40, 52), against the rendered ones elsewhere; the two אִישׁ-headed chains, *the ways of a man* (34.21) against the recast possessive *his ways* (34.11); *Who* on the waw at 34.8 against *Who* added at 34.7, where the juxtaposed finite clause carries no conjunction morpheme at all (rules 17, 55); כֹּל plus suffix at 34.13, where the noun is written and the suffix goes unrepresented under rule 22, against 34.19, where the suffix is the rectum and takes *they* under rule 19.

The two privative מִן shapes are licensed, not split. At 34.10 the מִן governs a noun and the ASV supplies a whole lexical verb, so the מִן keeps only *that* and *he should do* / *he should commit* are added under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause. At 34.30 the ASV writes the negation and a presentative frame for the recast clause and no negative morpheme stands to take them, so both join the מִן under rules 48 and 50. Both units in each verse are headed alike.

Copula placement is uniform across 34.4, 34.6, 34.7, 34.18, 34.19, 34.21 and 34.35: always on the predicate morpheme, prepositional under rule 49 or nominal and adjectival under rule 20, and never on an explicit or supplied subject. 34.29's *it be done* is not a counterexample, being a supplied passive with its own dummy subject rather than a copula the preposition beside it could take.

Fusion statuses divide 8 aligned to 2 noncompositional, and the division is principled: the two noncompositional units (34.20 חֲצוֹת לָיְלָה → *midnight*, 34.27 אֲשֶׁר עַל־כֵּן → *Because*) are exactly the ones whose source head rests on rule 6's deterministic first-token anchor. Recorded as a convention, not promoted, because the corpus records both statuses for the same fusions (לִפְנֵי → *before* is aligned 424 times and noncompositional 266) and a rule the corpus contradicts is worse than none.

BSB: all 11 disagreements are the documented convention differences and none is an error. Five are prepositions the ASV's recasting leaves nothing to say (rules 40, 52); three are paragogic he (rule 32); one is the directive he of 34.13, unrepresented because עַל already holds the relational word, which is rule 32's own sentence; one is the resumptive suffix of כֻּלָּהּ (rule 22); and one is the Ti prefix at 34.18, where the printed ASV renders no question at all and the margin recording the interrogative pointing was read and set aside under rule 38. Nothing was changed to move the rate.

No promotions or amendments. Everything this chapter decided was already reachable from the contract as it stands: 34.22's *Where* on the resumptive שָׁם is rule 22's own 'or with a resumptive adverb' clause, 34.18's *Him that* on a substantival infinitive is rule 46's headline 'anarthrous substantive' sentence, and 34.10's distributed *from ... from* is rule 25's מִן example verbatim.
